sentences.en: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.
sentences.zh: 但当你们看见耶路撒冷被兵围困，就可知道它荒凉的日子近了。

sentences.en: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those who are inside the city depart,
sentences.zh: 那时，在犹太的应当逃到山上，在城里的应当出来，

sentences.en: and let not those who are out in the country enter it, for these are days of vengeance to fulfill all that is written.
sentences.zh: 在乡下的不要进城，因为这是伸冤的日子，要应验经上所写的一切话。

sentences.en: Alas for those who are with child, and for those who give suck in those days, for great distress shall be upon the earth, and wrath upon this people.
sentences.zh: 当那些日子，怀孕的和奶孩子的有祸了！因为将有大灾难降在这地方，也有烈怒临到这百姓。

sentences.en: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive among all nations, and Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 他们要倒在刀下，被掳到各国去；耶路撒冷要被外邦人践踏，直到外邦人的日期满了。

sentences.en: Now, that was the top geopolitical pundit, Jesus Christ, making his debut on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是顶尖的地缘政治名嘴——耶稣基督，在《历史其余部分》节目的首次亮相。

sentences.en: It was a brilliant impression, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 模仿得太精彩了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's exactly how he spoke, actually.
sentences.zh: 对，其实他说话就是这个腔调。

sentences.en: To add to your roster.
sentences.zh: 为你的人才库再添一员。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I can do, so I can do Trump, Nixon, Margaret Thatcher, and Jesus.
sentences.zh: 我还能模仿特朗普、尼克松、玛格丽特·撒切尔和耶稣。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically covering Jesus.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上把耶稣也涵盖了。

sentences.en: And smugglers.
sentences.zh: 还有走私犯。

sentences.en: And smugglers, yes.
sentences.zh: 还有走私犯，对。

sentences.en: So, Tom, Jesus was right.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，耶稣是对的。

sentences.en: Jerusalem was surrounded by armies.
sentences.zh: 耶路撒冷被军队包围了。

sentences.en: People did flee to the mountains.
sentences.zh: 人们确实逃到了山上。

sentences.en: And Jerusalem was utterly crushed by the military might of the Roman Empire at the end of the Jewish revolt, which is the subject of today's podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在犹太起义末期，耶路撒冷被罗马帝国的军事力量彻底粉碎，这也是我们今天播客的主题。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically the story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，故事基本上就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: People can stop listening.
sentences.zh: 大家可以不用听了。

sentences.en: Or am I wrong?
sentences.zh: 还是说我错了？

sentences.en: Dominic, you're so wrong.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你大错特错。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a brilliant, a thrilling, terrible, blood-soaked story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其精彩、惊心动魄、惨绝人寰且血流成河的故事。

sentences.en: This episode is following on from the episode that we did for Easter on the crucifixion.
sentences.zh: 本期节目是接着我们复活节那期关于耶稣受难的节目往下讲的。

sentences.en: I'm not saying this is a sequel, but it kind of is a sequel in that this is about, just as the crucifixion was, in the long run, a seismic historical event.
sentences.zh: 我不是说这是续集，但从某种程度上说它确实是续集，因为正如耶稣受难从长远来看是一个震撼历史的重大事件一样，

sentences.en: So also is this revolt, this destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这场起义、罗马人对耶路撒冷的毁灭也是如此。

sentences.en: And it's one that far more than the crucifixion, of course, is recognized by contemporaries at the time as being of great significance.
sentences.zh: 而且，与耶稣受难相比，这场毁灭在当时更被同时代的人认为具有重大意义。

sentences.en: So right from the beginning, people who wrote about it said this is a war without parallel.
sentences.zh: 因此，从一开始，撰写这段历史的人就称这是一场空前绝后的战争。

sentences.en: Certainly, that was the perspective of one Jewish historian.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这也是一位犹太历史学家的视角。

sentences.en: And to the present day, people have said this is the key clash, not just in ancient history, but of all time.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，人们依然认为这是古代史上、乃至整个历史长河中最关键的冲突。

sentences.en: So in 1896, a New Testament scholar, the Bishop of Durham, a guy called B.F.
sentences.zh: 所以在1896年，一位新约学者、达勒姆主教，名叫B.F.

sentences.en: Westcott, said that it is no exaggeration to say that the fall of Jerusalem to the Romans in AD 70 is the most significant national event in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 韦斯科特的人说，毫不夸张地说，公元70年罗马人攻陷耶路撒冷是世界历史上最具有国家意义的事件。

sentences.en: Okay, well, that is an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这确实有点夸张了。

sentences.en: I mean, the beginning of a sentence was completely wrong, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那句话的开头就完全错了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or was he arguing that because it has this immense theological significance?
sentences.zh: 还是说，他之所以这么论证，是因为这具有巨大的神学意义？

sentences.en: It's because this is in the first century AD, and as your quotation from the New Testament suggested, this has an amazing significance for Christians.
sentences.zh: 这是因为事件发生在公元一世纪，正如你引用的新约经文所暗示的那样，这对基督徒来说具有非凡的意义。

sentences.en: But of course, it also has a huge significance for Jews because the climactic event in this war,
sentences.zh: 但当然，这对犹太人也具有极其重大的意义，因为这场战争的高潮事件——

sentences.en: the event that continues in a way to cast a shadow over politics in the Middle East to this day,
sentences.zh: 那个在某种程度上直到今天仍在为中东政治投下阴影的事件——

sentences.en: was the incineration of the temple, which was the great focus of Jewish life, Jewish ritual practice.
sentences.zh: 就是圣殿的焚毁，圣殿曾是犹太人生活和宗教仪式的核心所在。

sentences.en: And the loss of the temple continues to reverberate through into the present.
sentences.zh: 而圣殿的失去，其影响至今仍在回荡。

sentences.en: So I think you can absolutely make a case that the subject of today's episode is crucially important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你完全可以证明，今天这期节目的主题至关重要。

sentences.en: However, I think saying that it's massively important to both Jews and Christians does highlight a risk with studying the episode itself,
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为强调它对犹太人和基督徒都极其重要，确实凸显了研究该事件本身的一个风险，

sentences.en: which is that we back project that significance onto what actually happened.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们会把后来的重要意义投射到当时实际发生的事情上去。

sentences.en: Understood.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So maybe, Tom, what we should do, I know you want to tell the story and then revise the story.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆，也许我们该这样做——我知道你想先讲故事，然后再剖析故事。

sentences.en: So there's a great sense of mystery here for the listeners, because you're going to tell the story in the first half,
sentences.zh: 所以对听众来说会有一种强烈的神秘感，因为你在前半部分讲故事，

sentences.en: and then the second half, you're going to tell us why everything you basically said was wrong.
sentences.zh: 然后在后半部分告诉我们，你之前说的话基本上全都是错的。

sentences.en: No, I'm not going to say it's wrong, but I'm going to say that perhaps the traditional perspective on it doesn't entirely tell the whole story.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会说那是错的，但我要说的是，传统的视角或许并没有完全道出事情的全貌。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You're going to pile on the nuance.
sentences.zh: 你要加入各种细微差别了。

sentences.en: You've sold that in a more nuanced way than I wanted to sell it.
sentences.zh: 你对这事的包装比我想要的要更有深度。

sentences.en: I wanted to create a greater sense of jeopardy and excitement.
sentences.zh: 我本来想营造更多的危机感和刺激感。

sentences.en: But you've destroyed that, so that's fine.
sentences.zh: 但你把它给毁了，所以好吧。

sentences.en: So as punishment, what you should do now is give us a bit of context.
sentences.zh: 作为惩罚，你现在应该给我们补充一点背景。

sentences.en: So we're in the first century AD.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在处于公元一世纪。

sentences.en: No, I think we should actually go back a bit further than that.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得我们实际上应该再往前追溯一点。

sentences.en: Oh, this is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 哦，这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: All right, go back further.
sentences.zh: 好吧，往前追溯。

sentences.en: Where do you want to start?
sentences.zh: 你想从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Well, I want to start, those listeners who've heard our episode on Babylon will remember that the first temple had been built by Solomon,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想从——听过我们巴比伦那期节目的听众会记得，第一圣殿是所罗门建造的，

sentences.en: gets destroyed by the Babylonians in the 6th century.
sentences.zh: 在公元前6世纪被巴比伦人摧毁。

sentences.en: The people of Judah, the kingdom of Judah, get hauled away to Babylon.
sentences.zh: 犹大的人民，也就是犹大王国，被强行掳到巴比伦。

sentences.en: They then get allowed to return to their land, to Judah, by Cyrus, the king of the Persians.
sentences.zh: 后来，波斯国王居鲁士允许他们返回自己的土地，也就是犹大。

sentences.en: And they rebuild the temple on the great rock in Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 他们在耶路撒冷的大磐石上重建了圣殿。

sentences.en: And essentially, they live as law-abiding, tax-paying subjects of the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们作为波斯帝国的臣民，遵纪守法、按时纳税。

sentences.en: And they have been able to preserve their identity in a way that other peoples who'd been transported by the Babylonians or the Assyrians hadn't,
sentences.zh: 他们能够保持自己的身份，而其他被巴比伦人或亚述人迁移的民族却没有做到这一点，

sentences.en: because they have a body of scriptures, of teachings, what they call Torah, and a whole body of other teachings as well, histories of how God had given them their land,
sentences.zh: 因为他们拥有一部经卷、一些教义（他们称之为托拉），以及其他许多教义，包括关于上帝如何赐予他们土地的历史、他们应该如何行事、诸如此类的内容，还有预言。

sentences.en: of how they should behave, all kinds of things like that, prophecies.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的内容，还有预言。

sentences.en: And this corpus of texts, what in due course will come to be known as the Bible, enables them to preserve their identity in a way that other peoples had not.
sentences.zh: 正是这批文献——即日后来被称为《圣经》的典籍——使他们能够保持自己的身份，而其他民族则未能做到。

sentences.en: So the combination of returning to this land and this body of scripture enables them to trace their origins back to before the sack of Jerusalem by the Babylonians.
sentences.zh: 因此，返回这片土地与这套经卷的结合，使他们能够将自己的起源追溯到巴比伦人洗劫耶路撒冷之前。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm interrupting you now.
sentences.zh: 好了，我现在要打断你。

sentences.en: Do they call themselves Jews?
sentences.zh: 他们自称为犹太人吗？

sentences.en: I believe they don't.
sentences.zh: 我想他们没有。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: They do not.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 对，他们没有。

sentences.en: What do they call themselves?
sentences.zh: 那他们自称什么？

sentences.en: So they are the people of Judah.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是犹大的人民。

sentences.en: But over time, so in due course, the Persian Empire falls, gets conquered by Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，波斯帝国灭亡，被亚历山大大帝征服。

sentences.en: We've done that as well in an episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在另一期节目里也讲过这个。

sentences.en: Very much a friend of the show, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以说是本节目的老朋友了，对吧。

sentences.en: And so these people become absorbed into the Greek world, and they're known as Judeoi.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些人被融进了希腊世界，被称为“尤代奥伊”（Judeoi）。

sentences.en: So we-
sentences.zh: 所以我们——

sentences.en: Judeans?
sentences.zh: 犹太人？

sentences.en: We translate that as Jews, but a better sense would be Judeans.
sentences.zh: 我们把它翻译成犹太人，但更好的理解应该是犹太地人。

sentences.en: And I think it is, I think the problem with using the word Jew, the Jews, is that it brings a lot of medieval and modern baggage.
sentences.zh: 我认为，使用“犹太人”这个词的问题在于，它带有了很多中世纪和现代的历史包袱。

sentences.en: There are lots of Judeans still in Babylon.
sentences.zh: 当时巴比伦还有很多犹太地人。

sentences.en: In the Greek period, they start to migrate to Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 在希腊时期，他们开始向亚历山大港迁移。

sentences.en: Then when the Greeks' empires succumb to the Romans, they start to migrate to Rome.
sentences.zh: 然后，当希腊帝国败给罗马时，他们开始向罗马迁移。

sentences.en: These are still Judeans because they're still looking to the mother city of Judea, which is Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 这些人依然是犹太地人，因为他们仍然心系母城犹太，也就是耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: And this is nothing exceptional.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么例外的情况。

sentences.en: There are Greeks scattered all over the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 地中海各地散落着希腊人。

sentences.en: They're still Greeks.
sentences.zh: 他们依然是希腊人。

sentences.en: There are Romans who are scattered all over the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 地中海各地也散落着罗马人。

sentences.en: Their mother city is still Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们的母城依然是罗马。

sentences.en: So I think that if you call them Jews, and the title of this episode is Romans Against
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，如果你称他们为犹太人，而本期节目的标题是《罗马对阵》

sentences.en: Jews, it makes, it kind of gives it a slight sense of a kind of religious war that has been
sentences.zh: 《犹太人》，这会给人一种这是一场宗教战争的错觉，这种印象

sentences.en: very, very influential, but I think obscures the degree to which this is essentially a provincial revolt.
sentences.zh: 非常非常深远，但我认为它掩盖了这本质上只是一场地方叛乱的程度。

sentences.en: And therefore, perhaps not quite as exceptional as we might otherwise be led to think.
sentences.zh: 因此，它或许并不像我们想象的那样那么特殊。

sentences.en: All right, let's not leap out too much to that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，我们先别急着下这个结论。

sentences.en: So at what point does this territory, the area around Jerusalem, at what point has that been brought into the Roman orbit?
sentences.zh: 那么这片领土，也就是耶路撒冷周边地区，是在什么时候被纳入罗马势力范围的？

sentences.en: Because obviously, you said it was Alexander the Great and then the Greek world.
sentences.zh: 因为显然你刚才说过那是亚历山大大帝和希腊世界时期。

sentences.en: But then at the end of the BC period, the Romans are the superpower.
sentences.zh: 但到了公元前这一时期的末尾，罗马人成为了超级大国。

sentences.en: Judea, like most of the Eastern Mediterranean, has been fought over by the Cleopatra and
sentences.zh: 犹太，就像东地中海的大多数地方一样，一直在克娄巴特拉和

sentences.en: Octavian and stuff.
sentences.zh: 屋大维等人之间争夺。

sentences.en: And it's been brought into the Roman orbit.
sentences.zh: 并且它被纳入了罗马的势力范围。

sentences.en: Well, it's before that, before that, before that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这还要更早，更早，更早。

sentences.en: So Alexander's empire gets dismembered.
sentences.zh: 所以亚历山大的帝国四分五裂。

sentences.en: You have two great powers.
sentences.zh: 当时有两个大国。

sentences.en: You have the Ptolemies in Egypt, and you have the Seleucids based in Syria.
sentences.zh: 埃及的托勒密王朝，以及总部设在叙利亚的塞琉古王朝。

sentences.en: And Judea is basically the pivot.
sentences.zh: 而犹太基本上就是个枢纽。

sentences.en: So it's kind of endlessly fought over.
sentences.zh: 所以它不断成为争夺的目标。

sentences.en: And as the Seleucid and the Ptolemaic empires decline, so they are able to establish a kind of independence.
sentences.zh: 随着塞琉古和托勒密帝国的衰落，他们得以建立某种程度的独立。

sentences.en: The Judeans.
sentences.zh: 犹太地人。

sentences.en: The Judeans, yeah.
sentences.zh: 犹太地人，对。

sentences.en: And in fact, they become a very expansionist, almost imperialist power.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们变成了一个极具扩张性、几乎是帝国主义的国家。

sentences.en: So if you think of it, try and visualize a map.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想到这一点，试着在脑海中勾勒一幅地图。

sentences.en: Jerusalem is kind of just above the Dead Sea, south of that region.
sentences.zh: 耶路撒冷大致位于死海的正上方、该地区的南部。

sentences.en: So kind of the western flank of the Dead Sea is a region called Idumea that gets conquered
sentences.zh: 所以死海的西侧有一个叫伊杜梅亚的地区，被

sentences.en: by the Judeans and that the Idumeans basically get obliged to become Judeans, to worship the
sentences.zh: 犹太地人征服了，伊杜梅亚人基本上被迫成为犹太地人，去信奉

sentences.en: Judean God.
sentences.zh: 犹太之神。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: To live by Judean kind of laws and rules.
sentences.zh: 按照犹太地人的法律和规则生活。

sentences.en: They also wage war against the people who live to the north, who readers of the New Testament will remember from the parable of the Good Samaritan.
sentences.zh: 他们还对居住在北方的人发动战争，读过新约的人会从好撒玛利亚人的比喻中记起这些人。

sentences.en: These are people from Samaria who are – the Judeans hate them because they are kind of like a ghostly parallel.
sentences.zh: 这些人来自撒玛利亚——犹太地人恨他们，因为他们就像是一个挥之不去的幽灵复制品。

sentences.en: They also were to have the law of Moses and so on, but they don't regard Jerusalem as holy.
sentences.zh: 他们也信奉摩西律法等等，但他们不认为耶路撒冷是圣城。

sentences.en: And this infuriates the Judeans.
sentences.zh: 这激怒了犹太地人。

sentences.en: So they – at the beginning of the very end of the second century BC, they storm the Sumerian capital.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在公元前二世纪末期，攻占了撒玛利亚的首都。

sentences.en: They destroy its holy place.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了那里的圣地。

sentences.en: So the Judeans are kind of very – they're a minor power relative to the great Greek empires
sentences.zh: 所以相对于庞大的希腊帝国

sentences.en: and certainly to the Roman Empire, but relative to the kind of the mix of peoples in what you could call kind of the southern Levant.
sentences.zh: 以及绝对庞大的罗马帝国，犹太地人只是一个小国，但相对于你可以称之为南黎凡特的各种民族的组合，

sentences.en: They're a significant player.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个重要的玩家。

sentences.en: However, they prove powerless to withstand the might of Rome.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们在罗马的强大力量面前显得无能为力。

sentences.en: The guy who initially conquers them is Pompey the Great.
sentences.zh: 最初征服他们的人是庞培大帝。

sentences.en: So go on to become the great rival of Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 也就是后来成为尤利乌斯·恺撒伟大死对头的那个人。

sentences.en: He captures Jerusalem in 63 BC.
sentences.zh: 他在公元前63年攻占了耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: He goes into this great temple, which is so holy that only one man, the high priest of the
sentences.zh: 他进入了这座宏伟的圣殿，这座圣殿神圣至极，以至于只有一个人——犹太地人的大祭司，

sentences.en: Judeans, on one day can go into the Holy of Holies.
sentences.zh: 一年只能在一天进入至圣所。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be the place, the presence of the one God of the Judeans, of the Jews on earth.
sentences.zh: 这里本应是犹太人唯一真神在人间显现的圣地。

sentences.en: Pompey goes into it.
sentences.zh: 庞培走了进去。

sentences.en: He looks at it.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周。

sentences.en: He finds there's absolutely nothing there and is quite impressed.
sentences.zh: 他发现里面空无一物，对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: And so he essentially says, fine, pay us tribute, but you can continue to worship as you want.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上说，好吧，向我们纳贡，但你们可以继续按你们的方式崇拜。

sentences.en: He thinks that the Judean God is worth kind of sucking up to.

sentences.en: He basically equates him with Jupiter, with the supreme God of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他基本上把这位神等同于朱庇特，也就是罗马人的至高神。

sentences.en: And as you said, Judea then gets kind of caught up in the snarl that is the civil wars, but first between Caesar and Pompey, then between Octavian and Antony and Cleopatra.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，犹太随后陷入了内战的泥潭，先是在恺撒和庞培之间，然后是在屋大维与安东尼和克娄巴特拉之间。

sentences.en: And what Antony and Cleopatra do is to install a guy called Herod, who is an Idumaean, so from these people who've been conquered, but is absolutely, you know, I mean, he is a Jew.
sentences.zh: 而安东尼和克娄巴特拉的做法是扶植了一个叫希律的人，他是一个伊杜梅亚人，也就是来自这些被征服的民族，但他绝对——我的意思是，他是一个犹太人。

sentences.en: He's a Judean.
sentences.zh: 他是一个犹太地人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he rules as king and he very skillfully is able to jump ships.
sentences.zh: 他作为国王统治，并且非常巧妙地见风使舵。

sentences.en: So Octavian, the future Augustus, when he has defeated Antony and Cleopatra, summons
sentences.zh: 所以屋大维，即未来的奥古斯都，在击败安东尼和克利奥帕特拉之后，召见了

sentences.en: Herod and Herod says, yeah, you know, I was on the side of Antony and Cleopatra, but that's because I was so loyal to them and I will now be loyal to you.
sentences.zh: 希律王，希律王说，呃，你知道的，我曾经站在安东尼和克利奥帕特拉一边，但那是因为我对他们非常忠诚，现在我也将对你忠诚。

sentences.en: And so he gets allowed to continue reigning.
sentences.zh: 因此，他被允许继续统治。

sentences.en: No.

sentences.zh: 嗯，所以奥古斯都有一句著名的调侃，说他宁愿做希律王的猪也不愿做他的儿子，这倒是个挺不错的笑话。

sentences.en: So, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: And so Herod is a very brutal but effective king.
sentences.zh: 因此，希律王是一位非常残暴但高效的国王。

sentences.en: He's a great builder.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的建设者。

sentences.en: So he develops the temple.
sentences.zh: 所以他扩建了圣殿。

sentences.en: He builds it on a stupefying scale so that it's installed as one of the great wonders of the entire Mediterranean world.
sentences.zh: 他以惊人的规模建造了它，使其成为整个地中海世界的一大奇迹。

sentences.en: And it remains what it's always been, the great focus for Judean loyalty.

sentences.en: So it's very wealthy.

sentences.en: Herod also develops an overtly Roman city on the coast, which he calls, with kind of unctuous civility, Caesarea.

sentences.en: Caesarea.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: So this is a palace, not a citadel, not a castle.

sentences.en: But yeah, there are a pair of palaces there.

sentences.zh: 所以耶路撒冷的人民吓坏了。

sentences.en: And so that's where, um, Gallus attacks.
sentences.zh: 加卢斯抵达耶路撒冷，耶路撒冷这座城市，其城墙除了北部之外，都建立在非常非常深的山谷之上。

sentences.en: He, he forces his way through.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是加卢斯发起进攻的地方。

sentences.en: The outer wall, there are two further walls beyond, but rather than attack them, Gallus then withdraws and he withdraws through a pass called the Beth Haron pass.
sentences.zh: 他强行突破了外城墙，外面还有两道城墙，但加卢斯没有攻击它们，而是选择撤退，他经由一条名为伯和仑的关隘撤退。

sentences.en: And there he's ambushed and his army's wiped out.
sentences.zh: 在那里他遭到伏击，他的军队全军覆没。

sentences.en: And this is the worst disaster that Roman arms has suffered since the, um, the annihilation of Varus's legions by the Germans in the, uh, the Teuterberger foreSt.
sentences.zh: 这是自瓦卢斯的军团在条顿堡森林被日耳曼人消灭以来，罗马军队遭遇的最惨重的灾难。

sentences.en: And this absolutely means that the Roman war machine is going to now demand a brutal vengeance.
sentences.zh: 这绝对意味着罗马的战争机器现在将要求进行残酷的复仇。

sentences.en: So essentially everybody who's been involved in that, whether it's been the massacre of
sentences.zh: 所以基本上所有参与其中的人，无论是春天在耶路撒冷屠杀罗马守军的人，还是在从耶路撒冷通往海岸低地的山隘中伏击罗马远征军的人，

sentences.en: the Roman garrison in Jerusalem in the spring or the, uh, the ambush of the Roman expeditionary force in the past going down from Jerusalem, down to the lowlands on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们的手上都沾满了罗马人的鲜血。

sentences.en: They are all that, you know, their, their, their, their hands are dyed in Roman blood.
sentences.zh: 这意味着罗马绝对会要求进行可怕的报复。

sentences.en: And that means that, that Rome is absolutely going to demand a terrifying vengeance.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，简单问一下。

sentences.en: Tom, quick question.
sentences.zh: 在此之前历史上从来没有人成功反抗过罗马，对吧？

sentences.en: Never in history up to this point has anybody successfully rebelled against the Romans, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有先例。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no precedent for this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，日耳曼人有过，日耳曼人在，嗯。

sentences.en: Well, the Germans have, the Germans did in, um.
sentences.zh: 但那是一场起义还只是一种抵抗？

sentences.en: But was that a rebellion or was that just resisting?
sentences.zh: 是的，那算是一场起义。

sentences.en: Yes, that was kind of a rebellion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，罗马人认为他们构成了一个行省，嗯，但日耳曼人不同意。

sentences.en: I mean, they, the Romans thought that they constituted a province, um, and the Germans didn't agree.
sentences.zh: 日耳曼人不同意，但你看，在那之后，罗马对日耳曼展开的报复是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: The Germans didn't agree, but you see having, uh, in the wake of that, the, the, the reprisals that the Romans brought to Germany were devastating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们进行了一场规模堪称种族灭绝的针对日耳曼部落的战争。

sentences.en: I mean, they walked, they waged kind of genocidal scale wars against the German tribes.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以没有将其设为一个行省，唯一的理由是他们觉得不值得。

sentences.en: And the, the only reason that they didn't constitute a province was that they felt that it wasn't worth it.
sentences.zh: 但犹太地是值得的，因为它具有极其重要的战略意义。

sentences.en: But Judea is worth it because it's strategically very important.
sentences.zh: 犹太地很富庶。

sentences.en: Judea is rich.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 更加富庶。

sentences.en: Richer.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且它是一个绝对至关重要的核心枢纽。

sentences.en: It's, it's, and it's this absolutely kind of crucial hinge.
sentences.zh: 它是一个绝对至关重要的核心枢纽。

sentences.en: So you can't have a Roman province in Syria and Egypt and not have Judea.
sentences.zh: 所以你不可能拥有叙利亚和埃及的罗马行省，却不拥有犹太。

sentences.en: But, but I mean, quite aside from that, it's the insult to Roman prestige.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是我的意思是，抛开这些不谈，这是对罗马威严的侮辱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it may, it means that there is absolutely no alternative and no Roman would, would ever think otherwise except to, to, to absolutely crush the rebels into the duSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能，这意味着绝对没有退路，任何罗马人都会，都会毫不犹豫地，彻底将叛军碾为齑粉。

sentences.en: And the Judeans who have defeated Gallus and, and revolted, um, do we know what they are thinking?
sentences.zh: 而那些击败了加卢斯并发动叛乱的犹太人，嗯，我们知道他们在想什么吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do they think we could carry this off?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们觉得自己能成功吗？

sentences.en: We could beat the Romans and become independent or they, is it this sort of doomed fatalistic struggle against overwhelming odds?
sentences.zh: 我们能打败罗马并获得独立，还是说，这是一种在悬殊实力面前注定失败的宿命式抗争？

sentences.en: Well, the Judeans are like a bunch of ferrets in a sack.
sentences.zh: 嗯，犹太人就像麻袋里的一群雪貂。

sentences.en: So the rebels all hate each other.
sentences.zh: 所以叛军内部互相仇恨。

sentences.en: There are kind of various different factions, depending on whether they are from Galilee or
sentences.zh: 他们有各种不同的派系，取决于他们是来自加利利还是

sentences.en: whether they're from Idumea or whether they're from central Judea, uh, whether they're upper class or lower class, whether they are of the priestly class or not.
sentences.zh: 他们是来自以土买还是来自中犹太，嗯，他们是上层阶级还是下层阶级，他们是祭司阶层与否。

sentences.en: Um, on top of that, you have large, large numbers of Jews, of Judeans who absolutely side with Rome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除此之外，还有数量庞大的犹太人，那些绝对站在罗马一边的犹太人。

sentences.en: So the most notable of these is, um, the local King Herod Agrippa, um, who has a kind of tranche of lands that's not actually within Judea, but kind of on the margins of it, but
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的是，嗯，当地的希律·阿格里帕王，嗯，他拥有一片土地，这片土地实际上不在犹太境内，而是在其边缘，但是

sentences.en: has a kind of personal responsibility for the administration of the temple.
sentences.zh: 对神庙的管理负有一定的个人责任。

sentences.en: And so before the revolt breaks out, he turns up and he can sense the way that things are going.
sentences.zh: 所以在叛乱爆发前，他赶了过来，他能感觉到事情的发展方向。

sentences.en: And he says, guys, you mustn't do this.
sentences.zh: 他说，伙计们，你们绝不能这么做。

sentences.en: This is insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Who do you think you are?
sentences.zh: 你们以为自己是谁？

sentences.en: Look at the power of Rome, look at all the people that she has, has conquered who, you know, just don't go there.
sentences.zh: 看看罗马的力量，看看她征服过的所有人，你知道的，千万别去惹他们。

sentences.en: And Herod Agrippa and his sister, Berenice, with whom he's said to have had an incestuous affair, they see themselves absolutely as kind of devout Judeans, people who are pledged
sentences.zh: 希律·阿格里帕和他的妹妹贝勒尼基（据说他与她有过乱伦关系），他们绝对把自己看作是虔诚的犹太人，是宣誓过

sentences.en: to the upkeep of the temple, but also loyal servants of Rome.
sentences.zh: 要维护神庙，同时也效忠罗马的仆人。

sentences.en: And there are lots of people across Judea, you know, who, whose interests have been tied up with Roman rule, who think this is a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 在整个犹太地区有很多人，你知道的，他们的利益与罗马统治紧密相连，他们认为这是一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: So it's a very, very, it's a very vociferous state of affairs.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常非常，这是一个声音嘈杂的局面。

sentences.en: There are lots of rivalries.
sentences.zh: 有很多对立的派系。

sentences.en: There is in no sense a kind of united front.
sentences.zh: 根本谈不上什么统一战线。

sentences.en: You know, this is, this is very kind of Judean people's front or people's front of Judea.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这非常像是犹太人民战线或是人民犹太战线。

sentences.en: You know, these are people who do all hate each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些人确实互相仇恨。

sentences.en: So they're all busy squabbling.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都在忙着争吵。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Romans are getting ready to reconquer it.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，罗马人正准备重新征服这里。

sentences.en: And Nero is still emperor at this point.
sentences.zh: 而此时尼禄仍然是皇帝。

sentences.en: And so he appoints a guy called Vespasian, who is not of, you know, the reason that Nero
sentences.zh: 于是他任命了一个叫韦斯帕芗的人，他并不是，你知道的，尼禄

sentences.en: appoints Vespasian is that he's going to hand over a large number of battle-hardened legions to him.
sentences.zh: 任命韦斯帕芗的原因是他要将大量身经百战的军团交给他。

sentences.en: And he doesn't want anyone who might in any way be a threat to him.
sentences.zh: 而他不想找任何可能对自己构成威胁的人。

sentences.en: Vespasian is a relatively humble stock.
sentences.zh: 韦斯帕芗出身相对卑微。

sentences.en: He's from kind of farmland out beyond Rome.
sentences.zh: 他来自罗马远郊的农田。

sentences.en: He's a very proficient soldier.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常能干的士兵。

sentences.en: He's pretty dull.
sentences.zh: 他挺无趣的。

sentences.en: He has a kind of very coarse sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 他有一种非常粗俗的幽默感。

sentences.en: He has the expression, as someone says, of someone, he always looks as if he's having a straining
sentences.zh: 正如某人所说，他总是带着一种表情，他看起来总像是正在使劲

sentences.en: for a shit, is the phrase that someone, one person uses to describe his expression.
sentences.zh: 拉屎，这是某个人用来形容他表情的词句。

sentences.en: But he's popular with his men, and he's very effective.
sentences.zh: 但他很受部下欢迎，而且效率极高。

sentences.en: And he moves into Galilee, and he annexes it.
sentences.zh: 他进军加利利并将其吞并。

sentences.en: He essentially takes it very, very easily.
sentences.zh: 他基本上非常非常轻松地占领了这里。

sentences.en: There isn't much resistance.
sentences.zh: 没有太大的抵抗。

sentences.en: The main focus of resistance is a town called Jotapata, which is commanded by a nobleman of kind of priestly background called Yusuf, who is the son of Matthew.
sentences.zh: 抵抗的核心是一个叫约塔帕塔的小镇，由一个具有祭司背景的贵族指挥，他叫约瑟夫，是马太的儿子。

sentences.en: And they hold out.
sentences.zh: 他们坚守阵地。

sentences.en: Then the Romans storm it.
sentences.zh: 随后罗马人对其发起强攻。

sentences.en: Yusuf will later tell a story about how all the resistors decided that they'd all commit suicide, and they'd each take it in turn.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫后来讲述了一个故事，关于所有抵抗者如何决定集体自杀，并且他们轮流进行。

sentences.en: You know, one person will kill another, then so it would go on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个人杀另一个，然后以此类推。

sentences.en: And he and one other are left, and they decide that they'll surrender.
sentences.zh: 最后只剩下他和另一个人，他们决定投降。

sentences.en: And he is laden down with chains, brought into the presence of Vespasian.
sentences.zh: 他身上戴着沉重的铁链，被带到了韦斯帕芗面前。

sentences.en: And Yusuf says to Vespasian, you are going to become Caesar.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫对韦斯帕芗说，你将成为恺撒。

sentences.en: It has been prophesied in our scriptures.
sentences.zh: 我们的经文中已经预言过了。

sentences.en: And Vespasian, he's kind of torn between the skepticism of a kind of a guy who's come up from peasant stock and an absolute gullibility.
sentences.zh: 而韦斯帕芗，他在这类出身农民的家伙的怀疑精神和绝对的轻信之间有些纠结。

sentences.en: And he's kind of intrigued, but not sufficiently intrigued to let Yusuf go.
sentences.zh: 他有点好奇，但还没好奇到放过约瑟夫的地步。

sentences.en: So Yusuf gets chained up and taken away with all the other prisoners.
sentences.zh: 所以约瑟夫被戴上铁链，和其他囚犯一起被带走了。

sentences.en: And the campaign continues.
sentences.zh: 战役仍在继续。

sentences.en: However, what then happens is that in 68, the summer of 68, Nero is toppled and commits suicide.
sentences.zh: 然而，随之发生的是在68年，68年夏天，尼禄被推翻并自杀身亡。

sentences.en: And the Roman Empire implodes into civil war.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国陷入了内战的崩溃之中。

sentences.en: And in AD 69, it's called the Year of Four Emperors.
sentences.zh: 而在公元69年，这一年被称为四帝之年。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And the person who emerges from the Year of Four Emperors as Caesar is none other than Vespasian.
sentences.zh: 而从四帝之年中脱颖而出成为恺撒的人正是韦斯帕芗。

sentences.en: Oh, so Yusuf was right.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以约瑟夫是对的。

sentences.en: Yusuf is right.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫是对的。

sentences.en: And that summer of 69, when Vespasian decides that he is actually going to throw his hat into the ring and try and become Caesar, as part of this, he has Yusuf, the chains are
sentences.zh: 而在69年那个夏天，当韦斯帕芗决定真正放手一搏、试图成为恺撒时，作为其中的一部分，他让约瑟夫，卸下了

sentences.en: struck off and he gets brought into his presence and he gets strongly encouraged to tell everyone that he had prophesied that this was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 铁链，把他带到自己面前，并强烈鼓励他告诉所有人，他曾预言过这一切将会发生。

sentences.en: I saw this coming.
sentences.zh: 我早就料到了。

sentences.en: I saw it coming.
sentences.zh: 我早就料到了。

sentences.en: And so Vespasian is very into it.
sentences.zh: 所以韦斯帕芗对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: So there's a whole, all this kind of swirl of prophecies that a king will come out of Judea who will rule the world.
sentences.zh: 因此有各种各样的预言流传，说会有一位君王从犹太走出来统治世界。

sentences.en: And Vespasian thinks it's him.
sentences.zh: 而韦斯帕芗认为这个人就是他自己。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: And so he comes from a family called the Flavians.
sentences.zh: 所以他来自一个叫弗拉维王朝的家族。

sentences.en: So Flavian propaganda is very, very hot on this.
sentences.zh: 因此弗拉维王朝的宣传对这一点非常非常热衷。

sentences.en: They cite Judean prophecy to the effect that a king will come from Judea and rule the world.
sentences.zh: 他们引用犹太人的预言，大意是会有一位君王从犹太走出来统治世界。

sentences.en: And what these prophecies mean is Vespasian.
sentences.zh: 而这些预言的意思就是韦斯帕芗。

sentences.en: Okay, perfect.
sentences.zh: 好的，太完美了。

sentences.en: Tom, this is the perfect point to take a break.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，现在正是休息的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: We're in the summer of 69.
sentences.zh: 我们正身处69年的夏天。

sentences.en: Brian Adams is warming up.
sentences.zh: 布赖恩·亚当斯正在做热身。

sentences.en: So let's be really looking forward to making that joke.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们非常期待去开那个玩笑。

sentences.en: We will be back to get into the bloodthirsty heart of the drama of the Jewish revolt.
sentences.zh: 我们将回归，进入犹太起义戏剧中血腥残酷的核心。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll be back for the next episode and that will be on Thursday and we will see you then.
sentences.zh: 我们将回归下一集，播出时间是周四，我们到时见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.zh: 如需收听加长节目、提前解锁、无广告收听并加入我们的聊天社区，请访问 restishistorypod.com 注册。
